text: ATM Audience Dashboard · written Oct 30, 2026 · daily figures through Oct 28 · monthly figures Oct 1–27
Awards voting doubled the site, LinkedIn reached more on more posts, and collabs decided Instagram.

Moment Awards voting drew 4,768 people to the site and doubled sessions on September. LinkedIn impressions rose 10% on 56 originals, against about 38 in September, so reach per post fell and comments dropped a fifth. Partners reposted, but rarely with their own words, so the September lift all but vanished (1.02× against 1.28×). On Instagram, posts with an accepted collaborator drew four times the views of the rest, and only 11 of 36 had one. The newsletter list grew 64% on imports, and clicks per delivered email held.

Sources: LinkedIn page admin analytics, the Instagram professional dashboard, YouTube Studio and GA4 (read Oct 28), Supermetrics, beehiiv, monday.com and the TEAM ATM live links. Daily figures refresh each time the page opens; monthly figures are from the October report (Oct 1–27); the baseline audit at the end is from September.
The read · Oct 1 to Oct 27, 2026
What the numbers say, and what to do about it

One reading of the October report and the daily figures, checked against what the team changed and when. Each point cites the section that holds the evidence. Reads of why a post did well are hypotheses.

title: Awards voting doubled the site.
text: atm.media drew 11,159 sessions and 9,498 users in Oct 1–27, about twice Sep 1–27. The /vote page alone drew 6,108 views from 4,768 people, and episode pages still grew 13% to 3,355 views. Voting ran to Oct 30, after this window, so the full month will read higher. Whether voters stay as readers is the open question. (At a glance; B)

title: LinkedIn reached more on more posts; conversation fell.
text: Organic impressions were 46,621 for Oct 1–26, up 9.9% on Sep 1–26, and reactions rose 15.8%. ATM posted 56 originals against about 38, so reach per post fell, and comments dropped 20% to 119. Interview cuts averaged 1,195 impressions; the 24 Top 20 and voting posts averaged 339. Followers reached 4,164, +281 in 30 days. (At a glance; B; E)

title: Partners reposted, but rarely with their own words.
text: Reposts with commentary added 35 engagements to 1,608 organic across 16 posts checked: a 1.02× lift, against 1.28× in September, when WPP Media, Nancy Hall and Versant reposted with their own copy. The guest's own network still did the distributing on the best posts: Sharb Farjami (7,002 impressions) and Caitlin Coburn Winsor (17 comments, mostly colleagues). (C; E)

title: On Instagram, an accepted collab is worth about four times the views.
text: The 11 posts with an accepted collaborator averaged 1,634 views and 44 interactions; the 25 without averaged 412 and 11. Invites on 26 posts were never accepted. Account views were 56,366 in the 30 days to Oct 27, down 10.7%, and followers barely moved (8,297, +15). The Top 20 carousel was the month's best post (6,021 views, 25 shares), passed on by nominees. (At a glance; B; E)

title: The newsletter grew on imports; clicks held.
text: Active subscribers reached 13,794, up 64%, and 5,588 of the 5,753 adds were imports (3,045 of them on Oct 26–27, after the last send). The open rate fell to 34.4% from 43.4% as the list grew, while verified human clicks rose 48% to 354 and held at 0.53% of delivered email. (At a glance; B; 02)

title: YouTube is steady and found through search.
text: 3,160 views in the 28 days to Oct 27, all organic, 60% of them from YouTube search, and +27 subscribers to 131. Only 5% of views came from outside YouTube, so the site and newsletter are not yet sending viewers. (At a glance; B)

title: Ask for the collab and a first-hour comment in every live-links email.
text: An unaccepted Instagram invite does nothing, and 26 of 36 October posts went without one. Put "please accept the Instagram collab" and a like or comment in the first hour into the live-links email, and follow up after a day. Target: half of Instagram posts with an accepted collaborator.

title: Hand guests and partners repost copy on publish day.
text: The September lift came from partners reposting with their own words; in October they mostly did not, and the lift fell to 1.02×. Send a ready line they can post with the link, and check the Reposts list two days later.

title: Turn voters into readers.
text: After Nov 5, send the voters a welcome email and track their 30-day verified clicks apart from the imports, so the Awards traffic can be judged on what it leaves behind.

title: Post fewer sizzles and more people.
text: Interview cuts drew three to four times the impressions of the Top 20 and voting posts. Cap Top 5 and winner posts at one a day, and keep two interview cuts a week on LinkedIn.

title: Rest repeat guests and widen the bench.
text: Rest Michelle Crossan-Matos, Meredith Diehn and Barbara Peng on social after Nov 5. Book Publicis and IPG voices, and CPG and pharma marketers beyond PepsiCo and Organon.

title: Give every guest and partner the exact tag.
text: Put "@At The Moment Media (ATM)" and the page link in the ready caption you send them, so nobody picks the similar page from LinkedIn's autocomplete.

title: Check the tag before anything goes live.
text: Add one line to the go-live checklist: any tag of ATM points to the ATM page, not "At The Moment". Check partner drafts the same way when they share them.

title: Search for mis-tags every week.
text: Add a weekly step to the daily run: search LinkedIn for recent posts that mention "At The Moment" alongside an ATM guest, series or partner name, and list what it finds. Ask the poster to fix the tag while the post is fresh.

title: Watch the other page's follower jumps.
text: The daily run already reads the competitor table. Flag any week "At The Moment" gains followers without posting, and line it up with ATM's posts that week: a jump right after a big ATM post points to mis-tags or mis-follows.

title: Log what you find.
text: Add a "tagged to the wrong page" column to the tagging audit, so the count shows month to month and you can tell whether the fixes work.

title: Rob and Hannah: move the Supermetrics data connections to a shared ATM login.
text: GA4, Search Console and YouTube connect through Rob's personal Google login, and LinkedIn through Hannah's. Instagram already uses the ATM account. If a personal login is disconnected, the daily social pull, the weekly GA4 pull and the monthly run stop.

title: Hannah: share the live optimization log.
text: So each monthly run can read it directly. The testing tracker in monday.com feeds the Briefings tab once it exists.

title: Rob and Dan: make utm_content the content ID on every link.
text: Use the episode slug as utm_content whatever the source, so several UTM links to one piece of content add up to that piece. Keep a small lookup sheet for older links.

title: Matt: add episode-level site and YouTube pulls for partner profiles.
text: Add per-page GA4 sessions and per-video YouTube views to the scheduled pulls, matched to partners by episode URL and video title. Partner profiles in Briefings can then show site visits to each partner's episode pages and views of the full episodes.

title: utm_partner does not show in GA4 reports.
text: It is not a standard GA4 parameter, so it needs a custom dimension before partner data appears. utm_term is standard and unused.

title: Newsletter traffic lands in "Unassigned".
text: beehiiv tags it newsletter and the episode links use owned_audience; GA4 files both as Unassigned. Set the medium to email, or add a channel group that joins them.

title: Every GA4 event is marked as a key event.
text: Engaged sessions, bounce rate and conversions mean nothing until the default events are unmarked. The fix only works going forward.

title: The Looker subscriber card is stale.
text: It has read 5,642 since Aug 31 while beehiiv reports far more. Re-point it, or retire it in favour of beehiiv.

title: No search tracking on the new site search bar.
text: If it does not send a GA4 event, the searches people run on the site are lost each day.

title: Episode links on social cuts have no UTM of their own.
text: Without one, traffic from the link layer cannot be told apart in GA4.

title: Internal visits count as site traffic.
text: In the 30 days to Oct 18, 366 sessions came from Microsoft Teams, Office documents and the site editor, mostly the team and partners opening links. Add an internal-traffic filter in GA4 so they drop out.

title: One piece of content appears under several utm_content spellings.
text: GA4 shows the same episode as "Nick Primola - Group EVP...", "NickPrimola-GroupEVP..." and "Nick", and the Deloitte episode three ways. Taking utm_content from the episode URL ending fixes this going forward.

title: Episode pages cannot rank in Google.
text: About 190 of 220 episode pages show no search impressions. Add a title tag, meta description, video schema, publish date and transcript to the episode template, clean up the slugs, and submit a video sitemap in Search Console.

title: Imported newsletter subscribers get no welcome email.
text: The welcome flow has enrolled 12 people since July while thousands were imported. Turn on a welcome automation for imports in beehiiv, and decide on double opt-in for cold sources. Referral milestones are also not set up.

title: Instagram follower demographics are not read.
text: They need a Meta Business Suite login, which no current run uses.

title: No play counts per episode.
text: Vimeo is not connected, so sponsor recaps cannot show plays per episode or per partner series.

title: overview
text: Moment Awards voting ran from the Oct 6 Top 20 reveal to Oct 30 (extended), and the Awards are on Nov 5. Most of October's site traffic is voting.

title: overview
text: ATM posted about half again as many LinkedIn originals as in September, many of them Top 20 sizzles, so totals rose while reach per post fell.

title: B
text: October 2026 runs to Oct 27 (LinkedIn to Oct 26). The month closes out in the next run. LinkedIn months before July include no sponsored impressions on this chart.

title: C
text: Repost tracking began in September. October is the second month measured, on 16 posts' Reposts lists.
3,045 imported subscribers arrived on Oct 26–27, after the last October send, so their first opens and clicks fall in November.

title: Followers.
text: LinkedIn's own total was 4,164 on Oct 27. The daily follower chart tracks organic gains from a fixed starting point, so it reads lower; use it for the trend, not the total.

title: Engagement rate.
text: LinkedIn's own rate counts clicks. The Overview scorecards leave clicks out so months compare on the same terms.

title: Time windows.
text: Monthly figures cover Oct 1–27 (LinkedIn Oct 1–26), against Sep 1–27. Instagram and YouTube monthly reads use their 30- and 28-day windows. Daily figures run to the latest day each platform has reported.

title: Sources this month.
text: The October report read the platforms' own dashboards because the Supermetrics connection failed on that run. The daily and weekly pulls use Supermetrics, so a few figures differ slightly from the report.

title: Subscribers.
text: beehiiv's active count includes imported addresses, so list size alone overstates readers; verified clicks are the better measure.

title: LinkedIn collab posts.
text: Records disagree on whether the feature is live on the ATM page, and the Oct 6 check found no collab option. Until that is settled, no figure on this page assumes it.

title: "At The Moment".
text: A separate LinkedIn page with a similar name, not an ATM page. It stays in the peer set and is watched for follows and tags meant for ATM.
